edges.description: Ultra-processed diets drive excess energy intake and weight gain even when calories presented, energy density and macronutrients are matched.
Density of and proximity to unhealthy food outlets raises fast-food consumption and body mass index.

nodes.description: Chronic positive energy balance from excess caloric intake relative to expenditure leads to fat accumulation. Multiple regulatory systems (leptin, ghrelin, insulin) fail to restore balance.

evidence.reference_title: The role of leptin and ghrelin in the regulation of food intake and body weight in humans: a review.
evidence.snippet: Leptin is a mediator of long-term regulation of energy balance, suppressing food intake and thereby inducing weight loss. Ghrelin on the other hand is a fast-acting hormone, seemingly playing a role in meal initiation.

evidence.reference_title: The role of leptin and ghrelin in the regulation of food intake and body weight in humans: a review.
evidence.snippet: In obese subjects the circulating level of the anorexigenic hormone leptin is increased, whereas surprisingly, the level of the orexigenic hormone ghrelin is decreased. It is now established that obese patients are leptin-resistant.

evidence.reference_title: Ultra-Processed Diets Cause Excess Calorie Intake and Weight Gain: An Inpatient Randomized Controlled Trial of Ad Libitum Food Intake.
evidence.snippet: participants gaining 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.009) during the ultra-processed diet and losing 0.9 ± 0.3 kg (p = 0.007) during the unprocessed diet

evidence.reference_title: The impact of the consumer and neighbourhood food environment on dietary intake and obesity-related outcomes: A systematic review of causal impact studies.
evidence.snippet: the number of and distance to unhealthy food outlets increased the likelihood of fast-food consumption and higher BMI for children of any SES
